title: Tool Authorization
security_question: Does a tool request become a tool grant, or does CTRL-MCP-001 decide before the handler starts?
retest_support_detail: ATTACK and RETEST share the same known-ungranted lookup_customer_tier request. Profile is server-owned ExperimentContext. Process env is not mutated.

ATTACK.attack_objective: Send the catalog ungranted lookup_customer_tier request on the intentionally vulnerable ATTACK experiment and observe whether CTRL-MCP-001 fail-opens before the handler.
ATTACK.why_this_matters: A tool request is not a tool grant. INV-001: an agent cannot receive more authority than was delegated. This ATTACK specimen is labeled vulnerable so you can later RETEST the same request under defense.
ATTACK.what_will_change: A new run.id is minted. CTRL-MCP-001 records a labeled fail-open ALLOW. Telemetry is emitted for this execution only.
ATTACK.what_will_not_change: Coded allowed_tools, grants, catalog valid_scopes. The browser does not choose the tool, scope, resource, or profile. Splunk does not ALLOW or DENY.
ATTACK.security_property: REQUEST != GRANT. On this labeled vulnerable experiment the ungranted known tool is ALLOW then executed. That is not universal MCP bypass.
ATTACK.expected_evidence_defended: Not this ATTACK specimen. Defended lookup_customer_tier is the RETEST experiment.
ATTACK.expected_evidence_vulnerable: INTENTIONALLY VULNERABLE LAB PROFILE: ALLOW with a fail-open reason, mcp.started, handler_invoke_count=1, testbed.mode=ATTACK. ALLOW is not execution by itself — mcp.started is.
ATTACK.predict_before_launch: Before you click Launch ATTACK, write: will CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW or DENY, will the handler start, and if denied what evidence should exist?
ATTACK.attacker_influence: The tool name, requested_scope, and arguments. The attacker wants an ungranted tool treated as authorized.
ATTACK.defense_should: On this ATTACK specimen the lab is fail-open. The defense you will enable is the RETEST ExperimentContext (profile=defended), not Splunk.

BASELINE.attack_objective: Run the catalog granted lookup_policy request so later ATTACK evidence has a normal comparison.
BASELINE.why_this_matters: Zero BASELINE rows is not all-clear. You need the shape of a granted ALLOW + mcp.completed before judging an ungranted tool.
BASELINE.what_will_change: A new run.id. CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW tool_granted. Handler 1. mcp.completed.
BASELINE.what_will_not_change: The grant list. This is not lookup_customer_tier.
BASELINE.security_property: INV-007 evidence for a granted tool; not an unauthorized-invocation test.
BASELINE.expected_evidence_defended: testbed.mode=BASELINE, profile=defended, ALLOW tool_granted, handler_invoke_count=1, mcp.completed.
BASELINE.predict_before_launch: Before you click Launch, write: should lookup_policy be ALLOW, and should mcp.started appear?

RETEST.attack_objective: Replay the SAME lookup_customer_tier request on the defended RETEST experiment and prove the outcome changed because defense changed, not because the request changed.
RETEST.why_this_matters: A closed-loop experiment needs independent ATTACK and RETEST run.ids. Process-global profile mutation would leak between concurrent experiments.
RETEST.what_will_change: A new run.id, testbed.mode=RETEST, profile=defended, DENY tool_not_granted if CTRL-MCP-001 matches.
RETEST.what_will_not_change: The tool, requested_scope, arguments, and request fingerprint. Coded grants. Splunk still does not enforce.
RETEST.security_property: Same adversarial request + different server-owned configuration = different security outcome. Not universal tool-authorization resistance.
RETEST.expected_evidence_defended: DENY tool_not_granted, attempted=false, executed=false, outcome=prevented, handler_invoke_count=0, no mcp.started on a complete copy, testbed.mode=RETEST.
RETEST.will_reach_operation: On defended RETEST, the ungranted tool should not start the handler. CTRL-MCP-001 should DENY first.
RETEST.which_control: CTRL-MCP-001 at acmebank.mcp.authorize, before the tool handler. AcmeBank owns enforcement. Splunk does not.
RETEST.falsify: mcp.started after DENY, or ALLOW on this RETEST experiment, would falsify the defended prediction. Missing Splunk rows alone would not.
RETEST.predict_before_launch: Will the same ungranted request reach the handler? If denied, what evidence should exist? Does missing mcp.started alone prove prevention?

limitations: LOCAL EDUCATIONAL SERVICE. Attack Service is localhost and unauthenticated.
NOT PRODUCTION AUTHENTICATION. NOT MULTI-TENANT. NOT INTERNET-FACING.
CTRL-MCP-001 is a lab allow-list, not production MCP IAM.
JSON-RPC is in-process, not stdio/HTTP MCP transport.
RETEST DENY is not automatically SAFE.
HEC HTTP 200 is not searchable evidence.
Missing mcp.started is not independent proof of prevention.
ALLOW is not execution. DENY is not an incident.
DET-MCP-001 alerts only on DENY-then-start. ATTACK fail-open ALLOW is silent. Silence is not SAFE.
Studio tokens are not auto-bound to a fresh run.id.
Learning metadata is not security policy.
